correctness.rationale: The dark-state recurrence leaves precisely seeds 0 and 1 modulo four, with the stated normalizers. The factorial moments of b^2 give 16j(j−1)+12j and 16j(j−1)+20j; different residue classes remove interference. An independent 80-term coefficient recurrence at z=0.2 and 0.7 matched direct moments to 7.2e−15; the supplied verifier was only inspected. In the rotating frame write P=|psi><psi| and G(t)=gamma D[L_t], suppressing the irrelevant scalar phase of L_t. Then G_0 P=0 and X=G'_0 P=−gamma (|xi><psi|+|psi><xi|)/2 with xi=L_0^† L'_0 psi. In particular Tr(PX)=Tr(P G_0 X)=0. The trace Taylor polynomial is P+t²X/2+t³(G''_0 P+G_0 X)/6. The trace against P of G''_0 P is −2gamma(||v||²−|<psi,v>|²), with v=L'_0 psi. Squaring the polynomial therefore gives the coefficient 2gamma||v_perp||²/3. Here v=−i Omega cosh(r)b²psi and v_perp=v, giving the formula and strict positivity for Omega nonzero. The rotating-frame kernel equality gives the exact full-profile phase condition, not merely matching the first derivative. For each zero-balanced series its j-th coefficient is c/j+O(j^−2), so F~c log(1/(1−z)), F'~c/(1−z), F''~c/(1−z)^2; using 1−z=sech²r gives the constant 1/12 in the sequential limit. When Omega=0 the cubic coefficient is identically zero, rather than a nonzero asymptotic equivalent.
correctness.trace_domain_check: Finite sections alone do not justify differentiating an unbounded generator. In the rotating frame let f_R(n)=(1+∫_0^n eta(x/R) dx)^k, with nonincreasing smooth eta equal to one up to 1 and zero above 2. This observable is constant plus finite rank, increases to (1+n)^k, has f_R'≥0 and |f_R''|<=C_k f_R/(1+n)^2. The number-diagonal adjoint dissipator has downward and upward rates cosh²(r)n(n−1) and sinh²(r)(n+1)(n+2). Taylor differences leave the first derivative multiplied by 2[sinh²(r)(n+1)(n+2)−cosh²(r)n(n−1)], nonpositive for all sufficiently large n, and errors bounded by C_k f_R. The only off-diagonal terms have shift four and contain the central second difference of f_R times an O((1+n)^2) factor; their quadratic forms are bounded by C_k f_R as well. This bound is uniform in R; it also holds in finite sections (truncating upward jumps only reduces the diagonal contribution). Gronwall and monotone convergence propagate all polynomial moments from the initial tails for conservative weak density solutions. Compression to n<=N then differs from finite-section Lindblad evolution by a trace-norm forcing O(N^(2−k/2)): each missing shift touches n>=N−4, and the weighted tail bound follows by factoring rho through sqrt(rho) and applying Schatten Cauchy–Schwarz. The same estimate yields a conservative trace-norm limit of the finite sections by contractive comparison. The Taylor polynomial above is a sum of finite-rank dyads with exponentially decaying, polynomially weighted vectors. It has trace-norm equation residual O(t³); compressing adds only an exponentially small cutoff defect. Contractivity and integration give O(t^4) error after the section limit at each fixed r. This supplies the analytic control implicit in the frozen proof's finite-section argument, without assuming uniformity as r grows.

value.rationale: The known qualitative failure of protection does not quantify its onset. The coefficient distinguishes full protection from first-order matching, shows why no encoded superposition can remove a nonzero cubic term, and shows how increasing squeezing amplifies mismatched phase in the sequential limit. These are usable predictions within the stipulated generator, not claims about microscopic environmental control.
